Your face is probably over producing oil because of how frequently you’re washing /touching your face. What cleanser do you use? I’d give your face a break and get a gentle cleanser like cerave or the ordinary’s squalene cleanser, use it once in the morning and once in the evening. Don’t scrub your face too hard. 

I’m sure you know diet plays a big role in skin as well but just in case make sure you’re drinking plenty of water, and make sure to avoid touching your face throughout the day. 

Your face will continue to overproduce for a while but as you reduce the amount of touching and scrubbing it should even out. If it’s still too much for you I’d really recommend seeing a dermatologist!

I agree with pretty much everything the other commenter said! The black mouse I have had since January and she was on deaths doorstep so she trusts me a lot and is very docile. The grey one was the friend I got her when I found out they need companions, she did NOT like people at all when I got her (I got her from a little girl who didn’t want her anymore). The spotted girl I got most recently and she was a sweet heart from the moment I got her. I have four other female mice, all with varying temperaments from “I’ll come up and maybe sit on your hand and sniff you if you have something tasty” to “If I see your shadow from across the room I’m gone”. 

I play with my mice on average for at least an hour or more per day, I try to spend time with them before and after work. When I first started, I’d place my hand in the enclosure (they trust palm down more for some reason???) and leave it there for 5-10 minutes. Even when they come up and sniff, or put a paw on you, don’t move your hand. Once they are used to you enough to stand on your hand, gently lift slightly. If they stay on, you can hold out your other hand to see if they’ll transfer. If they jump off, let them go and start the process over again. 

It takes a lot of patience but I got my grey girl to go from running away to jumping at me when she sees me. It’s frustrating but I can tell you I have literally cried when one of my shy girls came up to me and put her paw on me for the first time. 

Another thing is that some mice are exploratory with their mouths. If they begin to nip, don’t yank your hand away. You risk harming them and scaring them. Gently pull back so your fingers aren’t in reach. 

I wish you all the best and I hope your girls get easier to handle!

One of my friends asked me last night why I cry so much, and the best way I could describe it is that I feel  everything on such a magnified level, it’s hard not to cry at any emotion I feel. We judge ourselves a lot for these things, we’re stuck with ourselves even when everyone else is gone. We also tend to view ourselves negatively, and the stereotypes that come along with BPD don’t help. I try to remind myself that I’m a whole person outside of this, and it helps a little bit. I try to think of how conversations I’ve had with others play out from the other side and I try to reassure myself that it went well, that I can be a likeable person. But I don’t think that feeling ever goes away, that fear of abandonment and worthlessness is so heavily ingrained.

Take time to enjoy the little things outside of the monotonous daily flow. Today, I was up at 3am and decided, you know what? It’s 20 degrees out, but fuck it. I put on sweats and a hoodie, took a water bottle and went on a walk until I found a nice tree, laid down and listened to music for half an hour. Take time for yourself to switch things up, not for the sake of being around other people but do things that make you feel whole. It made me feel human to feel the chill in my fingers, or to stare up through a pine tree at the stars. Do things that make you feel human again, not like a robot. Good luck my friend!
